readmeExcerpt:
Magnitude

Run powerful open models on the hardware you already own

Magnitude is an open source inference engine that spreads models across your GPU, RAM, and SSD so they run on everyday Macs and PCs. It works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, or just a CPU. One click connects it to the agent you already use (Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more). ⭐ Help us reach more developers and grow the Magnitude community. Star this repo! ## Get started Download the installer: - **macOS:** [Apple silicon](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=darwin&arch=arm64&package=dmg) · [Intel](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=darwin&arch=x64&package=dmg) - **Windows:** [x64](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=windows&arch=x64&package=windows-exe) - **Linux x64:** [.deb](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=x64&package=deb) · [.rpm](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=x64&package=rpm) · [.pkg.tar.zst](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=x64&package=pacman) - **Linux ARM64:** [.deb](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=arm64&package=deb) · [.rpm](https://magnitude.dev/api/installer?os=linux&arch=arm64&package=rpm) Setting up a server? Install the CLI only: ```sh curl -fsSL https://magnitude.dev/install.sh | sh # macOS / Linux irm https://magnitude.dev/install.ps1 | iex # Windows PowerShell ``` For more info, see [CLI only](https://docs.magnitude.dev/installation/cli-only). For Docker container installs, see [Docker](https://docs.magnitude.dev/installation/docker). ## Why Magnitude? - **Use your whole machine:** streams experts from RAM and SSD, not just your GPU - **Tuned to your chip:** optimizes kernels per model, over 2x faster than Ollama - **Works out of the box:** configures itself for your machine, no flags or manual tuning - **Built for concurrent agents:** flexing KV memory and shared prefix caches - **Works with your agent:** one click connects Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more - **Free, private, open source:** no token costs, nothing leaves your machine, Apache 2.0 ## How it runs on everyday hardware [View full benchmarks →](https://magnitude.dev/benchmarks) ## FAQ ### How does it run models bigger than my memory? Most large open models today are ultra sparse MoEs: they are split into hundreds of small parts called experts, and only ~5% activate for each token. Magnitude spreads the model into tiers (GPU VRAM holds the shared layers and most used experts, system RAM holds the next tier of frequently used experts, and your NVMe SSD holds the rest). On every token, Magnitude predicts and prefetches upcoming experts up from SSD to RAM to VRAM before the GPU needs them. ### Why is it faster than other local engines? Other engines ship one-size-fits-all kernels, because tuning each model for each chip by hand would take forever. Magnitude tunes kernels automatically on your actual chip when you download a model, pairs each model with its best speculative decoding drafter, and predicts and prefetches streamed experts off RAM and SSD ahead of time. [See the full benchmarks against Ollama.](https://magnitude.dev/benchmarks#ollama) ### What hardware do I need? Any Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel GPU, or nothing but a CPU, on macOS, Linux, or Windows (desktop app, headless CLI, or Docker). VRAM needs to fit at least the active experts for a model; beyond that, the more experts you can cache in VRAM and RAM the faster it runs, and a faster NVMe SSD (like PCIe 5.0) speeds up anything that spills to disk. Magnitude profiles your machine and recommends the best models before you download anything. ### Which models can I run? Any GGUF model from Hugging Face in a supported family, including fine-tunes and other people's quants. We write optimized kernels for each of the most popular open-weight families, including sparse MoE models that stream from RAM and SSD. See the families and the models we recommend at [magnitude.dev/models](https://magnitude.dev/models). ### Which agents work with it? One click connects Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Oh My Pi, and Cline. Anything else works through the OpenAI-compatible API. ### Will streaming wear out my SSD or slow down my computer? No. Streaming model weights from your SSD is strictly read-only, so it causes zero flash wear. Magnitude also uses direct uncached reads instead of OS disk swap, and dynamically shrinks KV memory when sessions go idle so your computer stays responsive. ### Is it free and private? Yes. Magnitude is 100% free and open source under Apache 2.0. Prompts, files, and models stay on your machine, with no token costs, API keys, or internet connection needed once a model is downloaded.
readmeHtml:
Magnitude

Run powerful open models on the hardware you already own

Magnitude is an open source inference engine that spreads models across your GPU, RAM, and SSD so they run on everyday Macs and PCs. It works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, or just a CPU. One click connects it to the agent you already use (Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more).

⭐ Help us reach more developers and grow the Magnitude community. Star this repo!

Get started

Download the installer:

  • macOS: Apple silicon · Intel
  • Windows: x64
  • Linux x64: .deb · .rpm · .pkg.tar.zst
  • Linux ARM64: .deb · .rpm

Setting up a server? Install the CLI only:

curl -fsSL https://magnitude.dev/install.sh | sh     # macOS / Linux
irm https://magnitude.dev/install.ps1 | iex          # Windows PowerShell

For more info, see CLI only. For Docker container installs, see Docker.

Why Magnitude?

  • Use your whole machine: streams experts from RAM and SSD, not just your GPU
  • Tuned to your chip: optimizes kernels per model, over 2x faster than Ollama
  • Works out of the box: configures itself for your machine, no flags or manual tuning
  • Built for concurrent agents: flexing KV memory and shared prefix caches
  • Works with your agent: one click connects Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more
  • Free, private, open source: no token costs, nothing leaves your machine, Apache 2.0

How it runs on everyday hardware

View full benchmarks →

FAQ

How does it run models bigger than my memory?

Most large open models today are ultra sparse MoEs: they are split into hundreds of small parts called experts, and only ~5% activate for each token. Magnitude spreads the model into tiers (GPU VRAM holds the shared layers and most used experts, system RAM holds the next tier of frequently used experts, and your NVMe SSD holds the rest). On every token, Magnitude predicts and prefetches upcoming experts up from SSD to RAM to VRAM before the GPU needs them.

Why is it faster than other local engines?

Other engines ship one-size-fits-all kernels, because tuning each model for each chip by hand would take forever. Magnitude tunes kernels automatically on your actual chip when you download a model, pairs each model with its best speculative decoding drafter, and predicts and prefetches streamed experts off RAM and SSD ahead of time. See the full benchmarks against Ollama.

What hardware do I need?

Any Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel GPU, or nothing but a CPU, on macOS, Linux, or Windows (desktop app, headless CLI, or Docker). VRAM needs to fit at least the active experts for a model; beyond that, the more experts you can cache in VRAM and RAM the faster it runs, and a faster NVMe SSD (like PCIe 5.0) speeds up anything that spills to disk. Magnitude profiles your machine and recommends the best models before you download anything.

Which models can I run?

Any GGUF model from Hugging Face in a supported family, including fine-tunes and other people's quants. We write optimized kernels for each of the most popular open-weight families, including sparse MoE models that stream from RAM and SSD. See the families and the models we recommend at magnitude.dev/models.

Which agents work with it?

One click connects Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Oh My Pi, and Cline. Anything else works through the OpenAI-compatible API.

Will streaming wear out my SSD or slow down my computer?

No. Streaming model weights from your SSD is strictly read-only, so it causes zero flash wear. Magnitude also uses direct uncached reads instead of OS disk swap, and dynamically shrinks KV memory when sessions go idle so your computer stays responsive.

Is it free and private?

Yes. Magnitude is 100% free and open source under Apache 2.0. Prompts, files, and models stay on your machine, with no token costs, API keys, or internet connection needed once a model is downloaded.

## 0.3.5

### Patch Changes

- [`80058fe`](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/commit/80058fead4cc41ad68d96a8ccb277b1f4721949b) Thanks [@anerli](https://github.com/anerli)! - Preserve multi-turn reasoning history and KV prefix cache across chat templates and multi-step tool loops.

- [#285](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/pull/285) [`66af400`](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/commit/66af4001ea076bee8d76508c56470317c15f1c70) Thanks [@dongreer](https://github.com/dongreer)! - Fix assessment of streamed Gemma 4 26B GGUFs failing with "a plan's tiers hold more than its weights" instead of Fits or DoesNotFit. releases.name: @magnitudedev/cli@0.3.4
releases.body:
## 0.3.4

### Patch Changes

- [`84c55f9`](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/commit/84c55f97be3eb65f71d0bd24130dc8c7bb501c40) Thanks [@anerli](https://github.com/anerli)! - Fix Windows 10 startup NUMA discovery, catalog drafter attribution, and streamed Gemma 4 CUDA startup panics.

  - Fixed startup panic on Windows 10 (builds prior to 20348) by requesting `RelationNumaNode` instead of `RelationNumaNodeEx` during host NUMA discovery ([#277](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/277), [#279](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/279)).
  - Fixed catalog drafter downloads (such as DSpark) being misattributed as their target model by including architecture in package identity and repairing stores that recorded one on load ([#280](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/280)).
  - Fixed CUDA startup assessment panic on streamed Gemma 4 26B-A4B partial expert banks by deriving each block's served decode split once and carrying it across certification, graphs, and runtime ([#276](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/276)).

releases.name: @magnitudedev/cli@0.3.3
releases.body:
## 0.3.3

### Patch Changes

- [`4dbdce0`](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/commit/4dbdce032e9b234a2ff2d07e7d568708dc7df663) Thanks [@anerli](https://github.com/anerli)! - Fix Windows memory sizing and iGPU/WDDM support, AMD RDNA3 Vulkan kernel crashes, Engram slab memory blowup, Apple Silicon startup crashes, and streaming decode throughput.

  - Fixed Windows CUDA VRAM budgeting via DXGI `IDXGIAdapter3::QueryVideoMemoryInfo`, stopped host-tier resize oscillation from fake trimmed RAM, and rejected mismatched shape-only drafter fallbacks ([#269](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/269)).
  - Fixed Windows host-tier startup starvation on tight RAM by reserving drafter head upload before bank growth and classifying host-staging shortfalls as insufficient memory instead of unsupported model ([#274](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/274)).
  - Enabled full shared system RAM grants on Windows integrated GPUs (such as Intel Arc 140V and AMD Strix Halo) and displayed shared memory in CLI/UI ([#275](https://github.com/magnitudedev/magnitude/issues/275)).
  - Fixed Apple Silicon 16 GB startup crash-loops (`assess.rs` fixed-point oscillation) via bracket

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source inference server that seamlessly connects AI coding agents to locally hosted models
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Magnitude is a localized inference server designed to bridge the gap between popular AI coding agents (like Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi) and locally hosted language models. It acts as a smart middleware that profiles the user's host hardware, recommends the optimal models that fit within local memory constraints, and automatically handles downloading and tuning. Once running, it exposes a standardized endpoint that existing agent software can plug into seamlessly. This enables developers to use powerful, automated agent tools entirely offline and privately, without relying on costly or privacy-invasive cloud APIs.
keyFeatures: Hardware profiling: automatically analyzes system resources to recommend models that fit within available RAM and VRAM.
Seamless agent integration: provides drop-in compatibility with popular coding agents like Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes.
Automated model management: handles the downloading, tuning, and execution of local models without manual configuration.
Offline execution: ensures all inference and data processing stays entirely on the local machine for maximum privacy.
Standardized API endpoint: exposes a uniform interface that mimics cloud providers, allowing existing tools to connect without modification.

useCases.title: Private Code Generation
useCases.description: Allows enterprise developers to use AI coding assistants on proprietary codebases without sending sensitive data to external cloud providers.

useCases.title: Offline Development
useCases.description: Enables engineers to utilize powerful AI agents while working on air-gapped systems or during travel without internet access.

useCases.title: Cost Reduction
useCases.description: Helps heavy users of AI coding tools avoid mounting API costs by shifting inference workloads to their local hardware.

useCases.title: Local Model Experimentation
useCases.description: Provides a streamlined way for developers to test how different open-source models perform with their preferred agent workflows.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Magnitude is built for software engineers, security-conscious organizations, and AI enthusiasts who want to leverage modern AI coding agents using their own hardware. It is ideal for users with capable local machines who prioritize data privacy and zero-cost inference.
